why: It reworks how legal documents and books get processed: the invoice job's fast path and hourly net, when issue_missing_credit_notes() runs, a new after() trigger on the seller-details save the executor must find, the ledger's turn order and an idle filter whose exists() list depends on which tables have a (store_id, time) index, Tripletex and Fiken narrowing, registry caps 'read from each function', and a CASE A/CASE B choice on a hot-table products marker with a trigger on product_translations and product_terms. Several of these are choices or readings the brief leaves open, and up to five migrations go to production through CI.
harm_if_wrong: An invoice or credit note that waits up to an hour or is never retried, a ledger book or accounting sync that silently skips new documents because an exists() clause names the wrong column, or extra writes on the hot products table from a new trigger.
make_it_cheaper: Split it into separate briefs (the eight indexes; the invoice job; the ledger turn; Tripletex/Fiken; the embeddings sweep) and decide case A or B once step 0.28 has landed, naming the exact exists() clauses and the seller-details save function; the index and invoice briefs would then be cheap-then-review.
brief_problems: The products text marker is written as two cases because step 0.28's result is unknown; in case B the trigger on product_translations and product_terms adds an UPDATE of commerce.products (a hot table) on every translation save, which the brief does not weigh.
The seller-details save to hook is left for the executor to find ('If the save function is not in this file, edit the file it is in').
Replacing commerce.store_is_active() with an inline join relies on the executor copying the function's body correctly; only the stop_if guards it.
The D-number instruction uses 'tail -1' without sort -n.
